$comment: research-analyst — the Research Analyst domain profile (founding spec §3, DOMAIN-PROFILE-SPEC-2026-11-09, ratified 2026-11-10): a financial model — a valuation / three-statement workbook — as the artifact. The dictionary is the transferability study's §4 map as data. Provenance discipline (spec §4): formula-derived edges are extracted_truth; market prices enter ONLY as source boundary nodes via sourced_from edges carrying source + as_of (both mandatory — the builder refuses an unsourced number); estimates enter ONLY through the estimates kind with method/window/error mandatory and never inside a core edge set; analyst judgment enters ONLY as a references edge carrying the claimant attr (declared_claim). RA is analysis-only, never advisory: this profile measures structure and arithmetic; it contains no recommendation, score, grade or verdict of any security. DATA DOCTRINE (settled, binding): Stooq is RA's declared production price source of truth; yfinance is development-only, never primary; no silent fallback — a missing Stooq series is an unmeasured field, never a number from another vendor; no production data routes to DeepSeek.

admission.notes: The four conditions, in words (the format stores the verdicts as booleans; the reasoning lives here and in the founding spec §3): (1) provable — a workbook's arithmetic is mechanically checkable, every output a function of declared inputs by formulas printed in the artifact, and the articulation identities are equalities that either hold or do not; (2) logic structure — double-entry articulation identities (assets = liabilities + equity; net income rolls to retained earnings; cash articulates across the three statements) and the formula dependency order are formal, checkable structure; (3) connectivity — the workbook is a formula graph by construction: every computed cell names the cells it reads, statements articulate by identity, scenarios bind to drivers, every market input binds to its source; (4) extractable truths — model-internally YES: every formula edge, containment edge and articulation identity is extractable from the artifact by rule, the formula text IS the rule. At the boundary the condition SPLITS honestly: a filed number is a sourced_fact (source + as_of), never an extracted truth; an analyst's forecast driver is an estimate with method/window/error; an analyst's judgmental link is a declared_claim with a claimant. Condition (4) therefore passes for the model's own arithmetic and is refused — by construction — for anything beyond it. inference is NOT admitted in v1: no edge in this profile may be inferred by a model or a heuristic; a correlation or factor loading is not a model-graph edge at all — it belongs to the separate estimates profile of the transferability study §6.2, which registers its own dictionary. Mixed RA graphs answer as claims-bearing by construction (§4.3): any answer whose walk crosses an estimates or declared_claim edge reports provenance_class per edge, and the graph as a whole classes claims-bearing under the engine's two-value §4.3 vocabulary (truths | claims-bearing) whenever any non-truth class is present. RA DATA DOCTRINE (settled, binding), declared here because the boundary def carries no policy field: a source is never part of the model's own structure — it is the filing, price series or dataset a number came from, named so the number can be re-derived. Stooq is the declared production price source of truth — a price enters only as a source node naming the Stooq series; yfinance is development-only and never primary, so a source naming yfinance is a development artifact and must not appear in a production graph; there is NO silent fallback — when the declared source has no series, the field is unmeasured (absent), never substituted from another vendor; no production data routes to DeepSeek. Sources never acquire dependency edges of their own and never appear in any edge set.

corpus: RA-F1: SEC EDGAR, Apple Inc. (CIK 0000320193), FY2023 + FY2024 10-K statements as filed — captured by the extractor stage (named in the contract's capture list)
RA-F4: RA engine seven-track outputs over RA-F1 — captured by the extractor stage
RA-F2/RA-F3: hand-auditable three-statement + DCF model and its three scenarios — authored by the extractor stage
RA-F5/RA-F6: broken-model and provenance mutation sets over RA-F2 — authored by the extractor stage
conformance.oracle: The RA Regression Contract (domain-profile build, stage3-evidence/CONFORMANCE-PLAN.md): fixtures RA-F1 (Apple Inc. CIK 0000320193 FY2023+FY2024 statements as filed, SEC EDGAR) and RA-F4 (the RA engine's own seven-track outputs over RA-F1) for engine parity (C-RA3); RA-F2/RA-F3 (the hand-auditable model and its scenarios) with hand arithmetic as the oracle for extraction, identities and both siblings (C-RA1, C-RA2, C-RA4); RA-F5/RA-F6 mutation sets for diagnostics and provenance behaviour (C-RA2, C-RA6); this probe (crates/codetopo-core/tests/ra_profile_probe.rs) as the mechanism-level oracle for R2 refusal and §4.3 taint until the extractor exists.
conformance.tolerances: Exact for counts, sets, orders, filed values and hand-arithmetic expectations; ratio arithmetic ≤ 1e-9 relative (C-RA3); articulation identities within each fixture's own declared tolerance in currency units (C-RA2) — tolerances are fixture inputs, never chosen by the runner.

edge_kinds.gloss: Structural containment ONLY: a model contains its statements; a statement contains its line items, drivers, parameters, periods and outputs (founding spec §1.4 — containment is never dependency and never enters an edge set).
edge_kinds.name: contains

edge_kinds.gloss: The formula edge — the calls analogue. The FROM cell's formula reads the TO cell: direction is reader → read, so dependents of a cell are the cells that read it (the hostage map: rank over computes_into answers 'which assumption is every output hostage to?'). The cell attr is the reading cell's own reference when the id does not already carry it.
edge_kinds.name: computes_into

edge_kinds.gloss: A statement-to-statement accounting identity, emitted as a DIRECTED PAIR (one edge each way) because the schema has no undirected edges (D7): net income computed on the income statement IS the net income that rolls into equity on the balance sheet; the cash line on the balance sheet IS the closing cash of the cash-flow statement. The identity attr names the identity asserted (balance_sheet_equation | net_income_rollforward | cash_articulation); tolerance is the declared rounding slack, in the model's currency units. The builder checks the identity over the two statements' measured values and a failure is a well-formedness finding (articulation_identity), never a silent pass.
edge_kinds.name: articulates

edge_kinds.gloss: A scenario binds the assumptions it sets: scenario → the drivers and parameters whose values it overrides. The scenario's own snapshot values live on the target nodes' measured fields in that scenario's graph; this edge records only the binding, so scenario_spread can diff the snapshots the bindings produce.
edge_kinds.name: assumes

edge_kinds.gloss: An input cell → the source boundary node its value came from: a filed statement line (SEC EDGAR filing), a market price series (Stooq — RA's declared production source of truth), a rate table. source and as_of are BOTH mandatory by the core provenance law: the builder REFUSES a sourced_from edge missing either (MissingProvenance). An unsourced number never becomes an edge — it is an unmeasured field: absent, never estimated. This is RA's own data-lineage rule (every input shows source + as-of) enforced by the builder instead of by convention.
edge_kinds.name: sourced_from

edge_kinds.gloss: The ONE place an estimate enters a model graph: an analyst's forecast driver or parameter applied to the cells it feeds (a projected growth rate feeding projected revenue). Class estimate; method, window and error are ALL mandatory — an estimate that cannot state how it was made, over what window, and with what error does not enter the graph. estimates is in NO edge set: no default core measure ever ranges over it, so an estimate can never silently hold an output hostage in a core answer; a graph containing it classes claims-bearing (§4.3).
edge_kinds.name: estimates

edge_kinds.gloss: RA's residue kind, live by its own declaration (D2): a reference the extractor found in the artifact that no rule above classifies — a cell mentioned in a note, a cross-reference in a model's text. When the reference is an analyst's judgmental link (this multiple is comparable to that peer's), the claimant attr is present and names who asserts it; the edge is then a declared_claim by the profile's per-edge rule and the graph classes claims-bearing while it is present. Without a claimant it is a found reference, class extracted_truth. Judgment is never dressed as truth either way: a claim is labelled a claim.
edge_kinds.name: references

methods.change_coupling: Two cells (or two statements) that change together across workbook revisions are coupled, exactly as two files that change together are. The transaction unit is the model: one saved revision of the workbook is one transaction. Pair counts transfer unchanged; the hotspot factor does NOT — a workbook has no complexity analogue — so no hotspot sibling is registered for this profile (declared absence, founding spec §1.4).
methods.hotspot: Not applicable to this profile: change coupling's pair counts transfer, its complexity factor does not. Declared absent rather than approximated.

id_grammar.boundary_stub: source::{source-name} — e.g. source::stooq:aapl.us:daily-close, source::sec-edgar:0000320193-25-000108 (an accession-numbered filing), source::filing:{cik}:{accession}

kinds.model: The workbook's own name as filed (e.g. aapl-dcf-2025) — the graph root.
kinds.period: {model-id}::period::{label} — e.g. fy2024, 2025q3; a period is a model-level node, not a cell.
kinds.scenario: {model-id}::scenario::{name} — e.g. base, bull, bear; a model-level node, not a cell.
kinds.statement: {model-id}::{sheet-name} — the sheet IS the statement (income | balance | cashflow | valuation), named by its role in the label.

id_grammar.notes: A cell id is the artifact's own coordinates, so the id and the location record never disagree: {model}::{sheet}::{CellRef}. Period and scenario are axes of the model, not cells, and carry their own segments. Source stubs live only under the boundary namespace source:: (per-profile namespace, governing default 7).

location.record: {artifact, sheet, cell}: artifact = the workbook/file name as ingested; sheet = the worksheet name; cell = the A1 reference (e.g. C42). For model-level nodes (model, period, scenario) sheet and cell are empty and the artifact alone locates the node. For source stubs the artifact is the source name and sheet/cell are empty.
location.unlocated: A node with an empty artifact has no physical location — the model root itself.

measured_fields.extraction_rule: The formula text exactly as stored in the cell (the workbook's own formula, verbatim, whitespace collapsed) — the signature analogue: it is the rule by which the cell's value derives, printed in the artifact. A hard-coded input cell has no formula and the field is absent — absent is never an empty string presented as a formula.
measured_fields.name: formula

measured_fields.extraction_rule: The cell's computed value at extraction time, recomputed by the extractor's evaluator from the artifact's own formulas — never the workbook's cached display value alone, and never a value the extractor supplied. A cell whose formula cannot be evaluated (a function outside the evaluator's set, a broken reference) carries NO value: absence is not_measured, never zero and never an estimate. Values from filed statements are the filing's printed numbers, entered as inputs under sourced_from edges — they are sourced facts about the source, recorded here as the cell's value with the edge carrying the provenance.
measured_fields.name: value

measured_fields.extraction_rule: The unit the artifact itself declares for the cell — its number-format currency (USD, CAD, EUR) or its sheet's declared scale (units | thousands | millions) — read from the artifact, never inferred from the ticker or the source. A model that declares no unit carries no unit: the field is absent and any cross-model comparison must say so.
measured_fields.name: unit

measured_fields.extraction_rule: The period label the artifact assigns the cell's column (FY2024, 2025Q3, LTM-2025Q3) exactly as printed in the artifact's own period row/column. A cell the artifact does not place in a period carries no period field.
measured_fields.name: period

node_kinds.gloss: The workbook itself — one financial model (a DCF, a three-statement model, a comps sheet) as ingested. The graph root and the history transaction unit: one saved revision of the model is one transaction.
node_kinds.name: model

node_kinds.gloss: One financial statement or valuation sheet of the model: income statement, balance sheet, cash-flow statement, or the valuation sheet that gathers the outputs. Statements articulate into each other by accounting identity (the articulates edges).
node_kinds.name: statement

node_kinds.gloss: One row-cell of a statement: revenue, COGS, operating income, total assets, operating cash flow. A line item is either an input (hard-coded, sourced) or computed by a formula from other cells (computes_into edges).
node_kinds.name: line_item

node_kinds.gloss: An assumption cell the model's arithmetic reads: a growth rate, a price, a volume, a margin. Drivers are where scenarios bind (assumes) and where an analyst's forecast enters (estimates) — the most hostage-worthy nodes in the graph.
node_kinds.name: driver

node_kinds.gloss: A model-wide constant the valuation reads: WACC, tax rate, terminal growth, discount rate, share count. Distinct from a driver: a parameter prices the whole model rather than driving one line.
node_kinds.name: parameter

node_kinds.gloss: A time axis node of the model (FY2024, 2025Q3, a forecast year). Periods organise columns; they carry no arithmetic of their own and sit outside every edge set — structure, not dependency.
node_kinds.name: period

node_kinds.gloss: A named assumption set (base / bull / bear, or an analyst's named case). A scenario binds the drivers and parameters it overrides (assumes); the spread of outputs across scenarios is the scenario_spread sibling's subject.
node_kinds.name: scenario

node_kinds.gloss: A cell the model exists to produce: equity value, per-share value, free cash flow, an implied multiple. An output is a MEASUREMENT of the model's arithmetic — never a recommendation: this profile records what the model computes, and nothing in it advises buying, selling or holding anything.
node_kinds.name: output

node_kinds.gloss: The boundary kind: a filing (SEC EDGAR), a price series (Stooq — the declared production source of truth), a rate table — anything outside the model that a number inside it came from. Sources are stubs under the source:: namespace; they are never contained and never carry the model's arithmetic.
node_kinds.name: source

siblings.citation: Transferability study §4 (RESEARCH-ANALYST-STUDY-2026-11-09): the sensitivity of an output to a driver is computed by re-evaluating the model's own arithmetic — perturbation of the input, re-evaluation of the formula graph — never by a fitted model of the output.
siblings.method_text: For an (output, driver) pair: perturb the driver's value by a declared step (default ±1% of its measured value, or one declared unit where the driver is a rate), re-evaluate every formula on the computes_into path from the driver to the output USING THE ARTIFACT'S OWN FORMULAS, and report the finite difference Δoutput/Δdriver and the elasticity (Δoutput/output)/(Δdriver/driver). The re-evaluation is the model's own arithmetic — no regression, no fitted surface, no external data. A pair whose path crosses an estimates edge is reported with its provenance class (estimate) named; a driver or output with no measured value is not_measured for this sibling, never interpolated.
siblings.name: sensitivity
siblings.oracle: RA Regression Contract fixture RA-F2 (the hand-auditable three-statement model): every (output, driver) finite difference recomputed by hand arithmetic from the fixture's printed formulas; the sibling must match the hand values exactly at the declared steps.
siblings.scope: Per (output, driver) pair connected by a computes_into path in one model's graph.
siblings.title: Sensitivity (∂output/∂driver by re-evaluation)

siblings.citation: Transferability study §4 and RA's own scenario practice (bull/base/bear cases are assumption sets over one model): the spread is a diff-family statistic over scenario snapshots of the same model — the same differencing discipline as the core diff measure, applied across the scenario axis.
siblings.method_text: For each output of a model: take its measured value under every scenario snapshot of that model (each scenario's assumes bindings applied, the model's own formulas re-evaluated), and report the set of values, their range (max − min), and each scenario's signed deviation from the base scenario. A scenario with no snapshot, or an output unvalued under a scenario, is named not_measured for that scenario — the spread is computed over the scenarios that measured it and says which. The spread is a measurement of the model's own dispersion across its declared cases; it is never a confidence interval and never a price target.
siblings.name: scenario_spread
siblings.oracle: RA Regression Contract fixture RA-F3 (one model, three declared scenarios): the per-output scenario values and spreads computed by hand from the fixture's printed formulas and scenario bindings; the sibling must match exactly.
siblings.scope: Per output, across all scenario snapshots of one model.
siblings.title: Scenario spread (output range across scenarios)

title: Research Analyst — financial model structure (statements, drivers, valuation)

well_formedness.name: research-analyst.balance_sheet_equation
well_formedness.rule: For every balance-sheet statement: total assets = total liabilities + total equity, over the statements' measured values, within the articulates edges' declared tolerance. A failure is a finding about the MODEL (its arithmetic does not articulate), reported with both sides' values — never silently repaired and never averaged away.

well_formedness.name: research-analyst.net_income_rollforward
well_formedness.rule: Net income measured on the income statement equals the net income that rolls into retained earnings on the balance sheet, joined by the articulates pair carrying identity=net_income_rollforward, within its declared tolerance.

well_formedness.name: research-analyst.cash_articulation
well_formedness.rule: The cash-flow statement's closing cash equals the balance sheet's cash line, joined by the articulates pair carrying identity=cash_articulation, within its declared tolerance; and opening cash + the statement's three section flows = closing cash inside the cash-flow statement itself.

well_formedness.name: research-analyst.single_valuation_output
well_formedness.rule: Core template: an output the model presents as THE equity value or THE per-share value is defined exactly once per (model, scenario). Two cells both presented as the model's per-share value are a multi_definition finding — the model contradicts itself, and the finding names both cells.

well_formedness.name: research-analyst.formula_resolution
well_formedness.rule: Core template: every cell reference in every formula resolves to a node in the graph. An unresolved reference is the financial #REF! — reported by cell, never dropped; a reference INTO the source:: namespace resolves only via a sourced_from edge, never as a formula read.

well_formedness.name: research-analyst.circular_reference
well_formedness.rule: Core template: a cycle in computes_into is a circular reference (the interest↔debt loop is the classic case). The builder reports the strongly-connected component by name; a cycle the model declares intentional (an iteration switch cell inside the component, named in the model's own text) is reported as a declared circularity — still a cycle, labelled, never silently evaluated.
